characters.name: atlas
characters.description: Use for planning, decomposing briefs into contract-valid Linear issues, dispatching Ready for Claude work, guarding the dependency graph and the credit budget, and merging what the gates pass. Never writes product code.

escalation.when: irreversible external action: DNS, domain, live Stripe keys, deleting tenant data
spend from the 5 percent reserve, or reversing one of the fifteen architecture decisions
hiring or retiring a character, the weekly release candidate, anything legal, tax or PCI
credential and account asks (Apple Developer, Windows signing, Twilio, Resend, Webflow, importer sandboxes), batched into one card
questions with a sensible default: anything a spec, ADR or rubric already decides
a session over 80 percent of its cap with no PR

characters.name: beacon
characters.description: Use for CRM pipeline and segments, email and SMS outreach sequences with compliance, the social scheduler with approval queue, Webflow landing pages, acquisition analytics, the support inbox and the content agent. Nothing reaches the public without human approval.

escalation.when: a CRM model change; a segment or filter grammar need; a platform adapter that cannot be built without an approved app; scope pressure on the five social adapters; any request to send outside the allowlist

every live send channel activation; every public post, email campaign or landing page before it goes live; platform developer accounts and app reviews; Webflow, Resend and Twilio account creation and billing; brand voice changes; consent policy
draft variants, CMS field mapping, sequence timing defaults, which OSS products to spike: anything a spec, ADR or rubric already decides
session at 100 percent of its cap: wip commit, footer, stop (PAP-111)

characters.name: forge
characters.description: Use for the paperos-template monorepo and its shells, Postgres, Drizzle, RLS and the typed API, local-first sync, Forgejo and mirroring, the VPS and deploy pipeline, Better Auth and the permission engine.

escalation.when: a contract another project consumes must change (API error shape, Principal, filter grammar, event envelope); two Forge sessions want the same package; a migration cannot be rolled back; a DoD needs a macOS or Windows runner; a library choice not covered by an ADR

Hetzner or DNS purchases; GitHub App installation on imagine-os; Apple Developer, Windows certificate and Android keystore; production migration windows; anything that deletes data or rotates the sops master key
version pins, folder layout, compose topology, which Base UI primitive to use: anything a spec, ADR or rubric already decides
session at 100 percent of its cap: wip commit, footer, stop (PAP-111)

characters.name: iris
characters.description: Use for DTCG tokens, the component library on headless primitives with Tailwind v4, themes per tenant, the motion system, Storybook, the component-to-spec mapping, and the portal and console shells.

escalation.when: a component another project needs that no issue owns; a codegen ui.* id with no component; a primitive library defect that forces a swap; a breakpoint matrix change; any request to add a CSS-in-JS runtime
brand identity choices with no token yet (logo, primary hue, typeface licence); a Figma seat or plugin purchase; any accessibility conformance claim published externally
spacing scale, component names, story structure, icon set: anything a spec, ADR or rubric already decides
session at 100 percent of its cap: wip commit, footer, stop (PAP-111)

characters.name: ledger
characters.description: Use for Stripe Billing, Connect and Tax, the double-entry ledger with hash chain, invoices and receipts, finance reports, the payroll provider adapter and the cash-flow data. Money code; an accountant will audit it.

escalation.when: any change to the Money contract; a posting rule that needs an account the chart lacks; a Stripe API version bump; a reconciliation that does not return zero after one investigation pass

Stripe live keys and account activation; Connect platform KYC; Stripe Tax registration decisions; the payroll provider sandbox agreement; the chart of accounts for the first real tenant; anything that files with a tax authority or moves real money
table names, trigger implementation, PDF layout, which report is a table view: anything a spec, ADR or rubric already decides
session at 100 percent of its cap: wip commit, footer, stop (PAP-111)

characters.name: nova
characters.description: Use for the table and views engine, multiplayer and realtime, the UX-flow canvas, the command registry and input abstraction, and the CRM, support and analytics surfaces that reuse those views.

escalation.when: a filter grammar or view model change; a schema change bigger than one table; a benchmark that misses budget by more than 30 percent after one optimisation pass; a library choice not in the registry; contention with Forge on packages/core exports
a licence for a commercial grid, chart or canvas library; a second load-generator host; any feature cut that removes a view kind from the 10-01 scope
keyboard model details, virtualisation strategy, which dagre or ELK layout, column widths: anything a spec, ADR or rubric already decides
session at 100 percent of its cap: wip commit, footer, stop (PAP-111)

characters.name: quill
characters.description: Use for page and app spec schemas and validator, review rubrics, the session playbook, the docs engine and ADR log, the prompt-log browser, the character handbook, memory curation, changelogs and the release digest.

escalation.when: two specs contradict each other; a spec requires a component or entity no issue owns; a rubric change would alter Gate 2 verdicts; a playbook change; an inbound issue that needs a product decision
product decisions surfaced by spec interviews; publishing anything externally; the release digest itself
wording, structure, section order, glossary terms, which example pages to document: anything a spec, ADR or rubric already decides
session at 100 percent of its cap: wip commit, footer, stop (PAP-111)

characters.name: scout
characters.description: Use to evaluate libraries and OSS products against the rubric, write adoption ADRs, maintain the registry and license policy, catalog MCP servers, run the weekly scan, and build importers and business templates.

escalation.when: a research time box about to be exceeded; a rubric or license policy change; an OSS product that should be forked rather than borrowed; a source API limit that makes an importer infeasible before 10-01; a scan candidate that would replace an adopted library
any paid licence or commercial plan; AGPL adoption; test workspace and sandbox accounts (Airtable, Notion, ClickUp, QuickBooks, Xero, Google OAuth), batched into one card; forking a whole product
scores, ADR wording, which five queries a scan uses, fixture design: anything a spec, ADR or rubric already decides
session at 100 percent of its cap: wip commit, footer, stop (PAP-111)

characters.name: sentinel
characters.description: Use for the four gates (static checks, Claude reviewers, screenshot and video inspection, edge-case hunting), security scanning, the threat model, flake quarantine, the eval harness and calibration. Blocks PRs; never merges.

escalation.when: a blocking finding the author disputes twice; a rubric or severity change; a gate red for infrastructure reasons for more than two hours; a critical security finding in merged code; calibration recall below the floor
a security incident involving real data or credentials; a waiver for a critical or high security finding; accepting a known accessibility failure into a release; the release candidate certification
individual review verdicts, flake quarantines, baseline updates for intended visual changes: anything a spec, ADR or rubric already decides
session at 100 percent of its cap: wip commit, footer, stop (PAP-111)
